title: R' Yeiva Saba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned several times in the Zohar. In Bereishit 59a, a man harbored doubts about the commandment of circumcision. R' Yeiva Saba fixed his eyes on him, and he became a heap of bones. Elsewhere the Zohar mentions “the aggadah of the school of R' Yeiva Saba.” This is what Seder HaDorot means in its entry Rav Yeiva, where it writes “R' Yeiva Saba והח׳”: its intention is “and he is a tanna,” because he is mentioned in the Zohar.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The second printed locator is האינו רצ.; it is retained exactly here, without silently correcting the section name or assigning a modern folio. The older OCR suggests האזינו, but that is not a fresh native reading. The initial locator בראשית נט. is conventionally 59a. The unclear shortened form והח׳ is kept in the quoted wording; Hyman himself explains its intended sense as והוא תנא, “and he is a tanna.” הסה״ד is rendered by the customary title Seder HaDorot, correcting the earlier Sefer HaDorot. Hyman’s explanation of that work’s label is attributed to him and has not been independently verified.

The personal titles abbreviated in Hyman remain R' here. The full Rav in the cited book-entry heading ‘Rav Yeiva’ is retained exactly as Hyman prints it; it is not transferred to the other occurrences. No exact Zohar title-bearing passage was checked, and the unresolved second locator remains unresolved.
